slides.headline: He measured a country's progress by what its people could actually do - not just its GDP.
Amartya Sen was born November 3, 1933, in Santiniketan, Bengal.
slides.body: In 1998, he became the first Asian to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, awarded for his contributions to welfare economics.

slides.headline: His 'capability approach' measures development by what people can actually be and do - health, education, freedom - not just income.
slides.body: That framework now underpins the Human Development Index and shapes how governments and economists worldwide think about growth that actually reaches people.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat built on Sen's framework is growth measured by capability, not just GDP.
slides.body: His insight - that development means expanding what people can actually do with their lives - is a quieter, harder standard than any single growth number.
